what_the_class_is: The mod delay as a whole: the stereo delay's two lines, loops, Fb Mode and damping, each line's read swept above its ladder entry by a modulator whose rate is the printed table and whose right side the Mod Phase byte sets apart, then the balance, level and tone stages.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A delay is a circular buffer addressed by a sample count, so a time is a whole number of samples and a tap is one more read of the same buffer; three or four taps cost three or four reads and no more memory.

A loop takes a read of the buffer, scales it and adds it to what is written, and damping in it is the cheapest pole there is -- one multiply and one state -- because it only has to take the top off the repeats.
Whether the value fed back is the read of this sample or of the last one is a question of how the program is scheduled, and either costs the same.
Times, rates, levels and corners are tables indexed by the byte, as the classes that read them closed on; a whole-type model borrows those tables rather than fitting its own.
era.would_be_wrong_if: The repeats of a held or struck note came back at spacings other than the ladder entry (or the entry and a sample) at settings nothing here was built on, or their level fell per repeat by other than the printed feedback times the damping pole.

candidates.reading: The modulator's shape (triangle). The loop returns straight off the line at the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: A pitch that holds two values a cycle and jumps between them, and a time of 0 has no order to be drawn in.

candidates.reading: The modulator's shape (triangle). The loop returns through a second read of the line one sample past the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: A pitch that holds two values a cycle, with every repeat a sample later than the ladder puts it.

candidates.reading: The modulator's shape (raised sine). The loop returns straight off the line at the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: A pitch that swings smoothly, the delay lingering at the ends of the sweep and at every depth 0.64 of the triangle's excursion; a time of 0 has no order to be drawn in.

candidates.reading: The modulator's shape (raised sine). The loop returns through a second read of the line one sample past the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: A pitch that swings smoothly at 0.64 of the triangle's excursion, with every repeat a sample later than the ladder puts it.

what_no_candidate_here_predicts: What the Mod Depth byte is worth on this type. The depth claim sets no law for a byte that swings a modulator, and the two takes walked on this type were refused by the reading at nearly every take, so the byte is read through the stereo chorus's pitch excursion -- the only depth curve measured on a swept delay line -- with no claim that the two types share it.
Whether the modulated read is interpolated otherwise than linearly: nothing here was asked about it.
What an Fb Mode value past 01 does beyond keeping the state 00, for the reason given on the stereo delay.
Anything at the addresses the page does not print: no node reads them, so every candidate renders them as the power-on state.
Whether the damping claim, closed on the stereo delay and checked on the mod delay, reaches this type's HF Damp byte: it is carried here unmeasured, one pole on the line's input inside the loop.
